title: Invocation Footprint Stitcher — export-first UX for per-call cost attribution
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design an export-first, compact UI for per-invocation cost attribution that lets engineers and finance teams slice, annotate, and export invocation-level spend. The 'Invocation Footprint Stitcher' is a lightweight pane that appears on route and model detail pages and supports: multi-dimension slicing (route, model, user_id, time bucket), attribution provenance (which token buckets, batching, cache hits contributed), CSV/NDJSON export with stable column schema, and on-demand sample replay links. Goals: 1) make per-call cost evidence discoverable and shareable; 2) enable finance and SRE to run quick audits without SQL or dashboards; 3) keep UI performant for heavy slices with progressive loading. Out of scope for this ticket: backfilling for >1 year windows, role-based export gating (handled in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria:
- Compact stitcher pane wireframes (desktop + mobile breakpoint) reviewed by PM & Eng.
- Prototype in Figma with state flows for slice selection, attribution legend, and export modal.
- Export schema defined and documented (CSV & NDJSON), sample file attached.
- Interaction spec describing progressive loading, error states, and sample-replay link behaviour.
- Accessibility checklist passed (keyboard nav, screen reader labels).
- Hand-off artifacts pushed to Confluence and a GitHub issue created linking design assets and dev tasks.
comments: 2025-02-11 — Initial scoping sync with PM (Ava Rodriguez) and backend (Ethan Liu). Decided: default slice = last 7 days, show top 100 invocations by cost. Backend will provide paginated API and precomputed attribution tags for first pass.

2025-02-18 — Early wireframes posted to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/invocation-footprint-stitcher. Feedback from Eng: prefer server-side sorting for top-k and return a deterministic 'sample_id' for replay. Added a sample-replay CTA design.

2025-02-24 — PM review: request to include a toggle for 'include cache-savings' since customers care whether KV cache reduced token bill. Added attribution legend with 'raw tokens', 'cache-missed', 'cache-saved', 'batching-overhead' categories.

2025-02-27 — Accessibility pass: updated color contrast for legend chips; ensured export modal receives focus and announces with ARIA. QA note: CSV column headers must be stable and documented for downstream ingestion.

2025-03-03 — Engineering sync: backend will expose a /v1/console/cost/invocations endpoint with query params (route, model, start, end, cursor, sort) and an export endpoint that streams NDJSON. Decided progressive loading: UI shows lightweight rows (summary) then expands detail on demand with attribute fetch.

2025-03-05 — Prototype link and export schema uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/COST/Invocation+Footprint+Stitcher. Created GitHub issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4832. Ready for design critique next week.
design_notes:
- Primary view: two-column compact pane. Left: faceted controls and time picker; center: top-100 invocations table with sparkline, cost, attribution badges. Expanded row shows token breakdown waterfall (prompt/response/kv-cache hits) and a compact diff if user compares two slices.
- Export-first pattern: Export button triggers modal where user selects columns, timestamp granularity, and format (CSV / NDJSON). Include 'Preserve IDs' toggle to keep sample_id for replay.
- Pricing UI pattern consideration: show both gross cost and normalized cost (cost after discount/commit) with tooltip explaining assumptions.
- Performance tradeoff: avoid fetching token-level diffs by default; fetch on expand. For CSV exports with deep detail, backend will stream results and the frontend will show a job modal with download link when ready.
- Edge cases: very large slices (>500k invocations) should show warning and suggest pre-aggregated export or time-window narrowing.
